# Psalm 101 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)
**Translator:** SOPHIA (Council Arbiter) | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A)

---

**1** A Psalm of David. I will sing of steadfast love and justice; to you, O LORD, I will make music.

**2** I will ponder the way that is blameless. Oh when will you come to me? I will walk with integrity of heart within my house;

**3** I will not set before my eyes anything that is worthless. I hate the work of those who fall away; it shall not cling to me.

**4** A perverse heart shall be far from me; I will know nothing of evil.

**5** Whoever slanders his neighbor secretly I will destroy. Whoever has a haughty look and an arrogant heart I will not endure.

**6** I will look with favor on the faithful in the land, that they may dwell with me; he who walks in the way that is blameless shall minister to me.

**7** No one who practices deceit shall dwell in my house; no one who utters lies shall continue before my eyes.

**8** Morning by morning I will destroy all the wicked in the land, cutting off all the evildoers from the city of the LORD.

---
## Council Notes

SOPHIA detected **6** significant divergence(s) in Psalm 101.

- **101:1** — EMET preserves Hebrew word-order; LOGOS restructures for English clarity; PNEUMA interprets for contemporary application.

- **101:3** — EMET preserves Hebrew word-order; LOGOS restructures for English clarity; PNEUMA interprets for contemporary application.

- **101:6** — EMET preserves Hebrew word-order; LOGOS restructures for English clarity; PNEUMA interprets for contemporary application.

- **101:7** — EMET preserves Hebrew word-order; LOGOS restructures for English clarity; PNEUMA interprets for contemporary application.

- **101:8** — EMET preserves Hebrew word-order; LOGOS restructures for English clarity; PNEUMA interprets for contemporary application.

- **101:4** — EMET preserves Hebrew word-order; LOGOS restructures for English clarity; PNEUMA interprets for contemporary application.

## Translation Notes (Select)

### EMET
- **101:2**: 'When will-you-come to-me?' — an abrupt cry in the midst of royal resolves; the king awaits divine presence to fulfill his ethical commitments.
- **101:8**: 'Every-morning' — justice administered daily at the city gate; the king's judicial responsibility is ongoing, not occasional.

### LOGOS
- **101:1-8**: A royal psalm — the king's 'oath of office,' pledging integrity in personal life (vv. 2-4) and public administration (vv. 5-8). It's a code of conduct for godly leadership.
- **101:5**: The sins targeted — slander, haughtiness, arrogance — are relational and systemic, not just personal. The king commits to shaping court culture.

### PNEUMA
- **101:2-3**: This reads like a king's personal mission statement: integrity at home, no tolerance for corruption, zero exposure to worthless things. It starts with private character before public policy.
- **101:6**: The king doesn't just avoid evil people — he actively seeks out faithful ones. Leadership is as much about who you surround yourself with as what you do.

— SOPHIA
